headline: Every bottle of gin checked, not a sample.
label: #F7F2E6
heroLede: Kilderkin opened in Ballarat in 2016, and its Larrikin gins are distilled, hand bottled and labelled there, from a classic dry gin to a 57% navy strength, with whisky now added. When gins of different strengths share a bottle, the label is what keeps the alcohol content right. This is what a camera check could look like when you bottle. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every bottle has its closure on, straight and fully seated, with the seal in place. A loose stopper means a leak in transit and a bottle that cannot be sold.
labelLede: An Australian gin and a navy strength gin in the same bottle look much the same, but one is a lot stronger, and the wrong label is a wrong alcohol statement. The camera checks every bottle carries the right label for the gin inside, straight and intact.
codeLede: The lot code ties every bottle back to its batch. The system reads the printed code on every bottle and compares it with the gin and lot set at changeover.
objectLede: Glass fragments, capsule offcuts and loose parts can end up on the bench. The camera spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four crooked closures in fifteen minutes. Check the capper.
